posts.title: Courts – Parent Company Update
posts.text: The Board of Courts (Ja) Ltd. wishes to advise the following: “The Board of Courts (Jamaica) Ltd announced on 3rd February, 2006 an update on the possible sale by Courts PLC (In Administration) of its controlling interest in Courts (Jamaica) Ltd. Exclusive negotiations with a preferred bidder with a view to finalizing the terms of a sale of the Courts Caribbean businesses including Courts’ interest in Courts (Jamaica) Ltd. are still continuing. The Transaction is subject to financing and signing of mutually agreeable legal documentation. The outcome of the discussions involving the Administrators and the providers of finance and the possible timetable for completion remain uncertain and could be protracted. However, the Board of Courts(Jamaica) Ltd. wish to clarify to its stockholders that, under the JSE Takeover Rules and applicable FSC regulations, any such sale will result in the purchaser becoming obliged to make an offer to all stockholders for all the shares of Courts (Jamaica) Ltd. The Board of Courts (Jamaica) Ltd. is preparing to respond on a timely basis to any offer for the company which may be made. Stockholders will be kept informed of relevant developments as they become known to the Board.”

posts.title: First Caribbean International Bank (FCIB) – Acquisition
posts.text: On January 31, 2006 the acquisition of ABN AMRO’s Curacao branch by First Caribbean International Bank became final. As a result, all banking and asset management activities in Curacao will be re-branded First Caribbean International Bank (Curacao) N.V. and First Caribbean Wealth Management (Curacao) N.V. respectively. This take-over will make FirstCaribbean one of the region’s leading providers of international banking services. Curacao is the seventeenth country in which FirstCaribbean will have established a presence in the last three years.

The Jamaica Stock Exchange will tomorrow (October 11) lift the suspension on the trading in the shares of Dyoll Group Ltd. which has submitted its second quarter financial report. This was announced today by JSE’s General Manager, Mrs. Marlene Street. The Board of the JSE had on September 16, 2005 decided to lift the suspension on the trading of shares in Dyoll Group Ltd. on or before October 11, 2005, if the company submitted its outstanding financial statements. The company has submitted its Group audited financial statements for the year ended December 2004 as well as its first quarter results. However, the second quarter results had been outstanding. Trading in Dyoll’s shares was suspended on February 15, 2005 because of its failure to provide material information to the JSE in keeping with the Exchange’s Policy Statement on Timely Disclosure (JSE’s Rule Book Appendix 8). Mrs. Street expressed satisfaction that the company’s report had met the Board’s deadline for submission and said that trading in the shares would resume on October 11.

posts.title: Dyoll Group Ltd. (DYOL)- Trading in Dyoll Shares Could Soon Resume.
posts.text: JSE’S BOARD CONSIDERS LIFTING SUSPENSION ON THE TRADING OF DYOLL SHARES The Board of the Jamaica Stock Exchange (JSE) on Wednesday, September 16, 2005 decided to lift the suspension on the trading of shares in Dyoll Group Ltd. on or before October 11, 2005, provided that the company submits its outstanding financial statements. Trading in Dyoll’s shares was suspended on February 15, 2005 because of its failure to provide material information to the JSE in keeping with the Exchange’s Policy Statement on Timely Disclosure (JSE’s Rule Book Appendix 8). JSE’s Executive Chairman, Roy Johnson pointed out that Dyoll Group has submitted its Group audited financial statements for the year ended December 2004 as well as its first quarter results. However, he said that the second quarter results were still outstanding. Mr. Johnson noted that the Board, at its regular monthly meeting this week, had deliberated on the matter and decided that once Dyoll was in compliance with JSE’s Rule 407 governing submission of ‘Quarterly Financial Statements’ the suspension of trading in Dyoll shares would be lifted on or before October 11, 2005. The Executive Chairman noted that the JSE remains resolute in pursuing its mandate in “providing a fair, efficient and transparent stock market” and ensuring the protection of all shareholders.

posts.title: JSE Suspends Trading of Dyoll Shares
posts.text: The Chairman of the Jamaica Stock Exchange (JSE) Mr. Roy L. Johnson, has today suspended trading in shares of Dyoll Group Ltd. The JSE has required that the Company make a public announcement in response to rumours that Dyoll Group has experienced material financial losses. This information has not been reported to the JSE in accordance with Appendix 8 (Policy Statement on Timely Disclosure). The Exchange in seeking to establish whether such rumours and speculation were factual or not, was informed by the Managing Director of Dyoll Group, Mr. Stephen Thwaites that he was estopped by the Acting Chairman, Mr. Peter Lawson from providing any information and was therefore not able to respond to the Exchange’s requirement that an announcement be made immediately by the Company. The Exchange advises that the suspension will remain in place until the relevant information has been disclosed.

posts.title: Sagicor Life Jamaica Limited (SLJ) – Acquisition
posts.text: LOJ declares that its mandatory cash take-over bid for ordinary stock units in PCFS has been accepted by Industrial Finance Holdings Ltd., British Caribbean Insurance Company Ltd. and Raiders Incorporated Ltd. This means that LOJ now controls more than 50% of PCFS and accordingly, the offer, which will expire on December 10, 2004, is now being treated as unconditional, subject only to regulatory approvals

posts.title: LOJ – Mandatory Cash Offer to Shareholders of PCFS
posts.text: Consequent on the acquisition of LOJ of the majority shares in Pan Caribbean Financial Services Ltd, the Board of Directors have now approved the acquisition of the minority shareholdings pursuant to the Rules governing takeovers and mergers of the Jamaica Stock Exchange.

posts.title: Capital & Credit Merchant Bank Ltd. (CCMB)- Acquires Majority Unit Trust Shares
posts.text: The Capital & Credit Financial Group (CCFG), comprising Capital & Credit Holdings Ltd. and Capital & Credit Merchant Bank Ltd., has been successful in its bid to purchase the 92.73% shareholding in the Jamaica Unit Trust Services Ltd. (JUTS) controlled by the Government of Jamaica. The Capital & Credit Financial GP was one of six firms which had tendered proposals for Government’s majority share of the Jamaica Unit Trust. The official take-over is set to be finalised very soon.

posts.title: Trinidad Cement Ltd. (TCL)- Director resigns
posts.text: At the Annual General Meeting of TCL Holdings Ltd. held on July 17, 2002 Mr. Arthur Lok Jack’s appointment as a director of the company was revoked, having regard to the loss of confidence in his ability to carry out his duties as a director of TCL Holdings Ltd. Mr. Lok Jack has tendered his resignation as chairman and director of Caribbean Cement Company Ltd. with effect from July 10, 2002. Mr. David Dulal-Whiteway, director, who retired by rotation, did not offer himself for re-election. Mr. Aleem Mohammed, director, who also retired by rotation, was not proposed for re-election.

posts.title: Caribbean Cement Company Ltd. (CCC)- Chairman Goes
posts.text: At the Annual General Meeting of TCL Holdings Ltd. held on July 17, 2002 Mr. Arthur Lok Jack’s appointment as a director of the company was revoked, having regard to the loss of confidence in his ability to carry out his duties as a director of TCL Holdings Ltd. Mr. Lok Jack has tendered his resignation as chairman and director of Caribbean Cement Company Ltd. with effect from July 10, 2002. Mr. David Dulal-Whiteway, director, who retired by rotation, did not offer himself for re-election. Mr. Aleem Mohammed, director, who also retired by rotation, was not proposed for re-election.

posts.title: Carreras Grp. Ltd. (CAR) – Offer for outstanding stock
posts.text: Following discussions with the JSE, British American Tobacco p.l.c.(BAT) announces that it will make an offer for the outstanding ordinary stock units of 25 cents each of Carreras Gp. at a price of JA$30 per stock unit. This offer will be made in compliance with Rule 19 of the Rules governing Take-overs and Mergers of the JSE. Subsidiaries of BAT now control 50.4% of Carreras. In accordance with the requirements of the JSE, the offer is at the highest price per stock unit paid by BAT to acquire 50% of the voting rights of Carreras Group. BAT operates in many countries around the world with minority shareholders and experience has shown that this arrangement is an effective way to maximize the returns on shareholder investment. While we are required to make this offer, in doing so we are not seeking to acquire any more shares in Carreras. BAT wishes to work with the management of Carreras for the long-term benefit of the group and all shareholders and would like to see Carreras remain a public listed company on the JSE. This offer will be made by a subsidiary of BAT and will be for the existing issued stock units together with all rights attaching to them at the date of this announcement or which subsequently become attached to them. The documentation containing the formal offer and the detailed terms will be circulated in due course.

posts.title: Salada Foods Ja. (SALF) – Trading Suspended
posts.text: The Council of the JSE has suspended trading in the shares of Salada effective Tuesday, March 30, 1999 for late financial reporting. The company’s audited financial statements for the year ended September 1998 were due on September 31, 1998. The suspension was effected pursuant to Rule 408 of the JSE Rules which states: “Companies with audited financial statements which are ninety days overdue shall have trading in their shares suspended until reports are submitted to the Exchange.” As soon as the outstanding statements are received the suspension in trading of the security will be lifted.

posts.title: Ciboney Gp. Ltd. (CBNY) – Trading Suspended
posts.text: The Council of the Jamaica Stock Exchange has suspended trading in the shares of Ciboney Gp. Ltd. effective December 1, 1997. The company’s audited financial statement for the year ended May 31, 1997 was due August 31. As soon as the outstanding statements are received the suspension in trading of the security will be lifted.
